title: Perspectives on Magnetic/Superconductor Hybrid Systems: Long-range Electromagnetic Phenomena Induced by Proximity Effect and Interfacial Spin-orbit Coupling
authors: S. V. Mironov, A. S. Mel'nikov, A. I. Buzdin
abstract: In this Perspective we review recent achievements in physics and applications of hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet structures. In particular, we focus on the manifestations of the electromagnetic phenomena in these systems originating from the response of the induced superconducting correlations modified by the exchange field and additional effects coming from the interface Rashba-type spin-orbit coupling. The review includes the long-range electromagnetic proximity effect and related modification of magnetic textures, spontaneous currents, properties of vortex matter and its interaction with magnetic ordering, spin-galvanic, photogalvanic and nonreciprocal transport phenomena in exemplary hybrid systems. We also present our views on the future development of this field including both the theoretical challenges and promising opportunities for fundamental experiments.
summary: This perspective review surveys the physics of superconductor-ferromagnet hybrids, focusing on how magnetic ordering and interfacial spin-orbit coupling induce long-range electromagnetic effects. It details mechanisms like the electromagnetic proximity effect, which leads to measurable magnetic field modifications in the superconductor. The work is crucial for understanding superconducting spintronics and developing novel quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper reviews the long-range electromagnetic phenomena occurring in hybrid superconductor-ferromagnet (S/F) structures, driven by proximity effects and interfacial spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
main_result: The review highlights the existence of a long-range electromagnetic proximity effect where superconducting currents penetrate the ferromagnet, inducing measurable magnetic fields in the superconductor.
method: The analysis involves reviewing theoretical models derived from electrodynamics (Maxwell's equations) applied to superconducting transport phenomena in layered magnetic structures.
model_or_system: The physical system is the S/F hybrid junction. Key mechanisms include the standard proximity effect, the electromagnetic proximity effect (where F magnetization induces screening currents in S), and SOC effects leading to nonreciprocal transport.
key_observables: Long-range magnetic field profiles ($B$), shifts in Fraunhofer critical current oscillations, and nonreciprocal transport signals (spin-galvanic, photogalvanic).
important_parameters: London penetration depth ($\lambda$), superconducting coherence length ($\xi$), and the magnetization ($M_0$) of the ferromagnet.
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on approximations such as the dirty limit or specific geometric assumptions regarding layer thicknesses relative to penetration depths.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetic field profile difference between separated and electrically contacted S/F layers, and show the expected shift in Fraunhofer critical current oscillations.
paper_structure: The review progresses by contrasting the competing orders of S and F, detailing the electromagnetic proximity effect, then focusing on the role of SOC in generating spontaneous currents, and concluding with discussions on future theoretical and experimental directions.
why_interesting: The interplay between superconductivity, magnetism, and spin-orbit coupling in nanoscale structures presents rich, non-equilibrium many-body physics relevant to open quantum systems and superconducting qubits.
